verses.text: Everyone should live under the governing authorities. No authority exists apart from God, and the authorities in place have been allowed by God.
So when you fight the authority, you’re pushing back against what God has established—and you’ll bring judgment on yourself.
Rulers aren’t a threat to people doing good, but to people doing evil. Want to have no reason to fear the authorities? Do what’s right, and you’ll have their approval.
The ruler is God’s servant, there for your good. But if you do evil, watch out: the sword isn’t there for decoration. The ruler is God’s servant, carrying out judgment against wrongdoing.
So submit—not just because you’re afraid of punishment, but because your conscience knows it’s right.
That’s also why you pay taxes: officials are God’s servants, putting in their time doing this work.
Give everyone what you owe: taxes to the tax office, customs to the customs office, respect to those due respect, honor to those due honor.
Don’t leave debts unpaid—except the ongoing debt to love one another. Whoever loves their neighbor has fulfilled the Law.
The commands—“Don’t commit adultery,” “Don’t murder,” “Don’t steal,” “Don’t covet,” and every other one—are summed up in this: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
Love doesn’t harm a neighbor. So love is how the Law gets fulfilled. ❤️
Do this with your eyes open: it’s time to wake up. Our salvation is closer now than when we first believed.
The night is nearly over; daylight is close. So let’s ditch the dark deeds and put on the armor of light. 🌅
Let’s live right out in the open—not partying hard or getting drunk, not in sexual sin or lust, and not in fights or jealousy.
Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ. Don’t set things up so your flesh can get whatever it craves.
